title: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca Bianca
subtitle: Spaghetti with anchovies, capers, olives, and no tomato
excerpt: A white version of the Neapolitan classic. Anchovy, capers, black olives, and garlic are cooked in olive oil until pungent and savoury, then tossed through spaghetti. No tomatoes, which makes the briny flavours sharper and cleaner.
sourceNotes: Variation on the Neapolitan puttanesca, omitting tomatoes to allow the preserved ingredients to lead. Synthesised from southern Italian pasta traditions.

content.text: This is a fast, very savoury pasta that needs barely any preparation. The anchovies dissolve into the oil and are not recognisable as fish. Taste before seasoning as the anchovies, capers, and olives bring a lot of salt between them.
Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to the boil. Add the spaghetti and cook until just under al dente, 1 minute less than the packet says.
While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a low to medium heat. Add the anchovies and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until they melt into the oil.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until the garlic softens but does not colour.
Add the capers and olives. Stir for 2 minutes. The mixture should smell intensely savoury.
Scoop out a large mug of pasta water before draining. Drain the spaghetti.
Add the spaghetti to the frying pan. Toss over a medium heat, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats every strand and looks glossy.
Remove from the heat. Add the parsley and a squeeze of lemon if using. Taste and add pepper. Salt is unlikely to be needed. Serve straight away.

items.symptom: The sauce is oily but not coating the pasta.
items.cause: No pasta water was added to emulsify the oil.
items.fix: Add 2 tablespoons of pasta water at a time and toss vigorously until the sauce becomes silky.

items.symptom: The garlic is bitter and dark.
items.cause: The heat was too high and the garlic went past golden.
items.fix: Start again with fresh garlic over a lower heat. Colour it just to pale gold, nothing more.

items.cause: The pasta water was too salty alongside the briny sauce ingredients.
items.fix: Balance with a good squeeze of lemon and a little extra pasta if you have it.
